subject.title: Model configuration accepts unvalidated model names, enabling silent misconfiguration

question: Should configured model-reference validation be advisory, strict fail-closed, or limited to known-retired/suppressed catalog entries?
rationale: OpenClaw policy treats config validation, provider routing, and fallback behavior as compatibility-sensitive, and source inspection shows the remaining fix depends on how much authority a catalog miss should have over custom or forward-compatible refs.

options.title: Advisory trusted-catalog validation
options.body: Warn in config validation and doctor when trusted runtime/catalog evidence cannot resolve a configured ref, while keeping custom and forward-compatible refs usable with clear wording.

options.title: Strict catalog validation
options.body: Reject any configured ref outside the trusted catalog, reducing runtime surprises but risking breakage for custom providers and newly released models.

options.title: Suppression-only validation
options.body: Keep current behavior limited to known retired or suppressed refs, preserving compatibility while leaving most of the reported class unresolved.

recommendation.title: Advisory trusted-catalog validation
recommendation.body: Warn in config validation and doctor when trusted runtime/catalog evidence cannot resolve a configured ref, while keeping custom and forward-compatible refs usable with clear wording.

likelyOwner.reason: Model/runtime history and release ownership make this the best available owner for the cross-cutting provider/config policy choice, with input from config and doctor contributors.
